slice.title: Add product stock adjustment action and availability labels
slice.goal: Extend the stock-enabled products-app prototype with an item-level Adjust Stock action and derived availability labels.
acceptance_criteria: Existing product catalog create, edit, list, name/SKU search, category filter, stock quantity, and availability filter behavior remains working.
User can open a compact Adjust Stock control from a product row/card without opening the full edit product form.
User can set a new stock quantity through the Adjust Stock control and see the changed stock quantity in the list.
Product list displays a derived availability label for each product: In Stock, Low Stock, or Out of Stock.
Availability filter behavior from SLICE-002 is preserved: in stock means stock_quantity greater than 0 and out of stock means stock_quantity equals 0.
The incremental run modifies the existing product catalog implementation instead of creating a separate stock or warehouse screen.
constraints: Use --from-run with a successful stock-enabled products-app run as baseline, for example runs/run-006-products-add-stock.
Preserve existing /api/products route and root product catalog screen.
Preserve existing name/SKU search, category filter, stock quantity create/edit, and availability filter behavior.
Prefer modify operations for existing product files over duplicate create operations.
Implement action.adjust-stock as screen-internal behavior inside the existing ProductCatalogScreen unless the approved file plan explicitly allows a separate artifact.
No inventory reservation, supplier integration, order management, stock history, or warehouse workflow.
Continue using local JSON mock storage.
non_goals: Inventory reservations, stock history, or audit log.
Separate warehouse or stock management screen.
notes: This scenario is intended to validate a second incremental modification through prepare_run_from_scenario.py --from-run.
The baseline should be a successful run of samples/products-app-add-stock, for example runs/run-006-products-add-stock.
This is an incremental scenario, not a greenfield product catalog.
Use it after a successful products-app-add-stock run to verify that the pipeline can preserve and extend already extended generated code.
